title: Epicyclic Gear System — Tabular Method
subtitle: The epicyclic (planetary) gear system is the most complex gear arrangement. One or more gears orbit around another gear. The tabular method is the cleanest way to solve these problems — and it always follows the same 3 steps.
learningOutcome: The epicyclic (planetary) gear system is the most complex gear arrangement. One or more gears orbit around another gear. The tabular method is the cleanest way to solve these problems — and it always follows the same 3 steps.

content.text: Here's the deal with epicyclic gears: the arm (the thing that holds the planet gears) can also rotate. This makes it confusing. The tabular method fixes that by breaking everything into 3 simple steps that always work.

items: Step 1: Fix the arm. Give gear A exactly +1 revolution. Fill in all gear speeds using gear ratio rules (−Z_A/Z_C for meshing gears).
Step 2: Now fix the arm. Give gear A exactly +x revolutions. Multiply entire Step 1 row by x.
Step 3: Add y to every element in every column. This accounts for the arm's actual rotation.

content.text: x and y are found by applying conditions (e.g. arm speed = y, fixed gear speed = 0 → set the gear's column = 0 and solve)
Speed of gear B in compound epicyclic
Z_A = teeth on gear A · Z_C, Z_D = teeth on intermediate gears · Z_B = teeth on gear B · y = arm speed · x = relative rotation

Common mistake — Forgetting to ADD y in Step 3 — students often just multiply by x and stop. The y term is the arm's absolute rotation, and without it, all your answers are relative, not absolute. Always do all 3 steps.

items: • Use the tabular method to find speed of any gear in an epicyclic system. Common exam Q
• Set up the table with 3 steps: arm fixed, arm rotates x, add y.
• Apply conditions (fixed gear = 0 speed) to find x and y, then solve.
